page: Amazon Web Services c8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The processor architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, alongside a 480 MB L3 cache.

Benchmark data positions this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded decompression, and software compilation. The memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth under large-block testing. In database and web serving workloads, the server achieves top-tier throughput, including high Redis SET operations and static web serving capacity. For artificial intelligence workloads, the hardware-accelerated matrix extensions enable top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds for small and medium-sized language models, despite the absence of dedicated GPUs.

The primary hardware tradeoffs of the c8i.metal-48xl include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and a relatively low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which may limit memory-bound applications. Single-core performance is moderate, falling into the average to strong categories. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal configuration eliminates virtualization overhead, making it highly resource-dense for compute-heavy, parallelized workloads. It is highly suited for high-performance computing, large-scale software compilation, batch processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server designed for high-throughput parallel workloads. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores running at 3.9 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of RAM. The x86_64 architecture includes Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, which drive top-tier multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations. While the server lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, its high-speed 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and top-tier memory bandwidth support data-intensive operations. Tradeoffs include a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core and moderate single-core performance. This instance is highly suited for compute-heavy workloads such as high-performance computing, multi-threaded software compilation, and CPU-based language model inference.
